name: Refused
label: Epitaph
lede: A Swedish hardcore band swore it would never play again, broke up mid-tour, made a record everyone hated, and spent two decades being proven right.

eras.title: Four kids in Umeå with a 7-inch to make
eras.text: Refused start in early 1991 in Umeå, a university town in northern Sweden, with a modest plan: play outside town and put out a 7-inch. Straight edge, vegan and loudly political, they grow up inside a tiny local scene that ends up feeding a lot of Swedish hardcore.

years.p: With guitarist Pär Hansson and bassist Jonas Lindgren, the band sets a small goal: get out of town and release a 7-inch.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band's formation to early 1991 in Umeå, with Lyxzén on vocals and Sandström on drums. The early records came out on small Swedish hardcore labels.

Lyxzén and Sandström are the two constants across every phase of the band, including the 2025 farewell.

eras.title: Straight edge, Marx and a Victory deal
eras.text: The first album and a run of EPs make Refused a fixture of European hardcore, and the second album pushes into metallic, more political territory. The band is by now a five-year-old project with a manifesto attitude.

years.h: This Just Might Be... the Truth, the debut album
years.p: Startrec and We Bite release Refused's first full-length, with Burning Heart on the credits too; the Everlasting EP came out the same year.
play: This Just Might Be... the Truth

years.src: Wikipedia: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent
years.h: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent: 12 songs in 30 minutes
years.p: Recorded in December 1995 with producer Pelle Gunnerfeldt, it opens with "Rather Be Dead" and adds screamed vocals to the band's attack.
years.xp:
The title borrows from the Industrial Workers of the World's Little Red Songbook, the 1909 collection tied to Joe Hill. It came out through Startrec and We Bite in Europe and Victory Records in the US.

Wikipedia gives 7 June 1996; the discography page gives 15 September. Used the season only.
play: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent

eras.title: The record that ended the band
eras.text: Refused decide, privately, that this is the last one, and try to make a record that no one can file under hardcore. Then it comes out, and hardcore hates it.

q: We could have called the record Fuck You.
years.h: Tonteknik, Umeå: recording The Shape of Punk to Come
years.p: With producer [[Pelle Henricsson|eb235754-f259-4d14-9122-4906905bda4a]], the band records on 24-track two-inch tape, mixing hardcore with jazz, electronics and strings.
years.xp:
Henricsson has said the album was made on tape, with no Pro Tools, and that groove was the guiding word. Lyxzén has said the band was on the brink of collapse and often its own worst enemy.

Louder reports that Sandström pushed for jazz, Brännström for electronics, and Lyxzén for surrealism and Situationist politics, which caused friction. Lyxzén says they could have titled it Fuck You.

years.h: The Shape of Punk to Come arrives on 27 October
years.p: Burning Heart puts out the record, subtitled A Chimerical Bombination in 12 Bursts, with "New Noise" as its centerpiece. Reviews and fans are mixed.
years.xp: Alternative Press called it the band's most hated record on release. Lyxzén said people told them that if this was the shape of punk to come, they were quitting punk.
play: The Shape of Punk to Come

years.big: Cut short by the police, and by the band
years.h: Harrisonburg, Virginia: the tour ends after a handful of shows
years.p: The band's last US show, in Harrisonburg, is shut down by police, and Refused announce they will never play together again.
years.xp:
Louder dates the show to 5 October and says police stopped it; another Louder piece says the split came on 6 October, three weeks before release. The band's statement ended with a promise never to play together again.

Wikipedia describes the tour as emotionally devastating and lasting about eight shows.

years.h: The New Noise Theology EP appears anyway
years.p: Burning Heart releases The New Noise Theology E.P. as the band is already gone.

eras.title: Dead, and getting bigger
eras.text: Refused stay broken up for 14 years. After Refused, Lyxzén fronts The (International) Noise Conspiracy, and Refused's reputation grows from a cult item into a reference point.

years.h: After Refused, Lyxzén fronts The (International) Noise Conspiracy
years.p: Lyxzén keeps political rock going with [[The (International) Noise Conspiracy|97da5eb3-79a5-4195-b98e-3d10ef946b08]] while Refused stays dead.

years.cap: Refused no Optimus Alive, Lisboa. · Wikimedia
years.h: Refused Are Fucking Dead: Steen's film about the last year
years.p: Guitarist [[Kristofer Steen|63064f8f-5d22-4862-b729-11f7dab678b0]] directs a 38-minute documentary on the band's final year, released in Scandinavia on 19 April 2006.
years.xp: The title nods to one of Refused's own songs and to Born Against Are Fucking Dead. The DVD adds live footage of nearly all of The Shape of Punk to Come and two music videos.

eras.title: Coachella and the second life
eras.text: The band that swore it would never play again does exactly that, and the crowds are huge. Then comes a new album, and a firing that gets public.

years.p: The reunited band plays its first show in its hometown before touring the US and Europe.

years.cap: Refused at Coachella, April 2012. Photo needed.
years.h: Coachella, two weekends: the reunion goes public
years.p: Refused play Coachella on 13 and 20 April, their first major reunion shows, despite having said they would never play together again.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls the decision controversial given the band's original statement. Alternative Press cites the album's later acclaim as a reason for reuniting.

Europe follows: Groezrock (29 April), Way Out West (9 August), Pukkelpop (18 August), plus Download, Rock am Ring, Hellfest and Roskilde.

years.h: Umeå homecoming at Exel Arena closes the reunion run
years.p: A show at Exel Arena, with a same-night afterparty at Fabriken, ends the 2012 tour.

years.h: Jon Brännström is out of the band
years.p: He says on Facebook in 2014 he got no explanation; the others say he did not share the band's passion.
years.xp:
Consequence reported that Brännström was let go in 2013 and revealed it on 31 October 2014. The band replied on 3 November 2014 that he did not share their passion for the band.

Brännström said he preferred studio work to touring.

years.h: Freedom, the first Refused album in 17 years
years.p: Epitaph releases it, produced by Nick Launay, Shellback and Michael Ilbert, after sessions in Los Angeles and Stockholm.
years.xp:
Singles "Elektra" (27 April), "Françafrique" (26 May) and "Dawkins Christ" (11 June) came first. The band released "Elektra" pay-what-you-want for Save the Children's Nepal earthquake relief.

Freedom reached number 2 in Sweden and number 161 on the Billboard 200 per Wikipedia.

eras.title: War Music and the farewell
eras.text: Refused go on with a bassist and a second guitarist added to the core, make one more record, and then decide to say goodbye properly.

years.h: War Music: the record people wanted last time
years.p: Produced by Sandström and Steen, with drums recorded on Gotland and the rest at Studio Kobra in Stockholm.
years.xp:
Lyxzén called it the record people wanted from Freedom. A European tour with Thrice followed in autumn 2019 and a North American run with METZ and Youth Code in early 2020.

The same year the band recorded music as the fictional band Samurai for Cyberpunk 2077, with Lyxzén singing.

years.p: Lyxzén sings the fictional band Samurai's songs for the game, credited to Refused.

years.h: Last show ever: Kulturväven, Umeå, closing on New Noise
years.p: After a farewell tour across North America and Europe, Refused finish at home on 21 December 2025 with a 95-minute set.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that members then formed Backengrillen with saxophonist Mats Gustafsson, whose debut album came out in January 2026.
